scope: PLC/LUTRAM structural research; not a runtime model or completed hardware validation

rules.claim: Each PLC2 has four slice views, eight LUT4 and eight fabric FF. Split BELs and coarse SLICE BELs are alternative interfaces, not additive capacity.
Local F50B11 belongs to SLICEA.MODE DPRAM, SLICEB.MODE DPRAM and SLICEC.MODE RAMW. These settings are coupled.
Physical LUT INIT addresses use A as bit 0, B bit 1, C bit 2 and D bit 3.
nextpnr distributed-RAM read address connects RAD0 to D, RAD1 to B, RAD2 to C and RAD3 to A; INIT indices swap address bits 0 and 3.
RAMW uses the eight A/B/C/D input contacts of slice C; its eight outputs feed four shared write-address lines and four data lanes for A/B.
Both A/B LUTRAM slices share WCK from CLK1 and WRE from LSR1. WREMUX and LSR1.LSRMUX share a CRAM bit.
The nextpnr packing view uses four LUT storage columns, two C placement blockers and one RAMW descriptor for a 16x4 memory in one PLC.
RAMW excludes normal C combinational functions in nextpnr; RAMW_BLOCK is a placement marker and the writer skips it. FF compatibility is checked separately.
There are two raw CLK and two LSR routes with per-slice selections. nextpnr imposes additional tile-wide FF compatibility restrictions; those are not a silicon legality proof.
The optional 96 LUT permutation arcs per PLC are routing-tool metadata. The writer changes INIT accordingly; they must not become 96 extra physical shorts in bitstream emulation.
Eight CCU2.INJECT1 positions also encode F-output route choices; interpret routing with mode context.
All 128 LUT INIT logical positions use inverted CRAM bits in the current PLC2 database. CRAM zero is not an all-zero LUT table.
The installed DPR16X4C legacy software model initializes addresses 0 through 14 only; address 15 is unknown until written. TRELLIS_DPR16X4 initializes all 16.
Distributed-memory read clocks, read enables and reset of generated output registers are fabric logic around the primitive.

open_questions.question: Datasheet PDPR16x4 requires six slices, while nextpnr packs independent read/write addresses into one three-slice PLC memory structure; measure the actual construction and distinguish primitive/IP semantics.
Available FF and extended-mux functions during RAMW/DPRAM, and behavior of nonstandard mixed mode settings.
Physical read-during-write, simultaneous observation and unknown-address/enable behavior; public models alone are not a silicon oracle.
INIT, configuration startup, GSR/local reset and retention of the LUTRAM array versus surrounding FF.
Physical constraints of shared CLK1/LSR1, inversion and separate FF clock/reset selections versus conservative packing rules.
Mode-qualified output mux and carry/LUT-extension behavior for overlapping control patterns, including chain boundaries.
Confirm all 16 initialized addresses on hardware while retaining the known legacy software initialization hole as a separate issue.
Confirm logical address, INIT permutation and live-write correspondence on native LUT contacts without applying routing-tool permutations twice.
The datasheet mentions level-sensitive registers, but the current PLC2 settings and inspected TRELLIS_FF model do not establish their configuration; investigate before excluding latch behavior.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Constrain independent RAD/WAD16x4 to one PLC with A/B DPRAM and C RAMW; change RAD while writing a different WAD, preserve routed-net and CRAM manifests.
hardware_cases.observe: All four data lanes, independent address behavior and occupied native resources.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Use asymmetric INIT and walking address bits at all 16 addresses; repeat with live writes and independent reads, including address 15.
hardware_cases.observe: Native A/B/C/D contact values, physical INIT index, logical data and the distinction from the legacy software-model hole.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Sweep both write-clock polarities, WREMUX passthrough/inverted/constants and shared FF reset/clock settings; vary inputs away from and then around edges separately.
hardware_cases.observe: Written location/data, inactive-edge retention and effects on FF sharing controls.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Read the written address and a different address during controlled write phases, repeating identical trials.
hardware_cases.observe: Observed output transition ordering and collision variability; do not infer universal guarantees from one stable result.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Pair LUTRAM with FF in A/B/C/D; independently apply local LSR, GSR and startup sequences while retaining a memory fingerprint. Test any level-sensitive candidate only after its configuration binding has been identified.
hardware_cases.observe: Which array/FF states change, resource compatibility and shared-control interactions.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Use explicit LOGIC/CCU2/DPRAM/RAMW patterns and identifiable LUT/carry outputs; check LUT5/6/7/8 and next-PLC boundaries in separate builds.
hardware_cases.observe: Active outputs and paths for each recorded CRAM pattern, with uncertain combinations retained as undocumented.
